title: Operational Strategy & Incident Support
description: Expertise spanning aviation operations, fire chemicals, communications, and strategy & tactics.
summary: Operational strategy and incident support from consultants who have held these roles in the field, not just studied them from the outside.
body: Wildfire and emergency incidents move fast, and the decisions made in the first hours often shape everything that follows. Our consultants bring aviation operations, fire chemical, communications, and strategy and tactics expertise built over careers in command roles, not as outside observers, but as people who have run these operations themselves.

Before the season starts, we help agencies and organizations build out aviation operations plans and airspace coordination, and shape retardant and fire chemical programs from the ground up. Once an incident is underway, that same expertise carries into incident communications architecture and tactics review on complex, fast moving incidents, giving command staff an outside, experienced perspective exactly when it's needed most.
The goal is always the same: give decision-makers clear, field-tested options, not theory.
credentials_note: Our consultants hold ICS qualifications including Incident Commander Type 1 (ICT1), Operations Section Chief Type 1 (OSC1), Air Tactical Group Supervisor (ATGS), Air Operations Branch Director (AOBD), and Helicopter Coordinator.

title: Policy & Program Development
description: Policy creation, review, and implementation aligned with best practices and organizational objectives.
summary: Policy and program work grounded in what actually holds up in the field, built by consultants who have written and lived under the policies they're helping you develop.
seo_description: Policy and program work grounded in the field, built by consultants who have written and lived under the policies they help you develop.
body: Good policy has to survive contact with a real incident. We help agencies and organizations draft new policy, review existing programs against current best practices and interagency and regulatory standards, and carry that work through implementation and the change management it takes to actually make it stick, not just a binder that sits on a shelf.

Our team's experience includes leading interagency policy efforts and program rewrites at the state and national level, giving us a practical sense of where policy tends to break down and how to write it so it doesn't.

Whether you're standing up a new aviation program, running an existing one through an audit against current best practices, or updating one that hasn't kept pace with your operations, we work alongside your team through drafting, review, and rollout.
credentials_note: Team experience includes leading initiatives such as the CAL FIRE Aviation Policy Rewrite Committee and the National Interagency Aviation Committee.

title: Training & Exercises
description: Design and delivery of Aviation ICS, field training assignments, and customized training programs.
summary: Training designed and delivered by consultants who have taught these courses and led these positions themselves.
body: Readiness is built long before an incident starts. We design and deliver Aviation ICS training, field training assignments (FTAs), and tabletop and full-scale exercises, with curriculum built around your organization's specific operations, risk profile, and agency requirements.

Because our consultants have served as instructors and evaluators in these same programs, training sessions are built around realistic scenarios and the judgment calls that actually come up in the field, not just a checklist of requirements.
We can build a standalone course, a full curriculum, or an ongoing exercise cycle, depending on what your team needs.
credentials_note: Includes consultants with direct experience developing and instructing at programs such as the California Aerial Supervision Academy.

title: AAR & Continuous Improvement
description: Facilitated after-action reviews to capture critical lessons learned and translate findings into actionable safety enhancements.
summary: Facilitated after-action reviews that turn a difficult incident into a clear, actionable path forward, led by consultants with command-level experience running the reviews themselves.
seo_description: Facilitated after-action reviews that turn a difficult incident into a clear path forward, led by consultants with command-level experience.
body: Every incident, successful or not, has lessons in it. Our facilitated after-action reviews (AARs) are built to surface those lessons honestly, without turning the process into a blame exercise, and to turn them into clear lessons-learned documentation and specific, trackable safety enhancement recommendations.

Our consultants have served in command and general staff roles, including Operations Section Chief and Type 1 Incident Commander, on significant incidents, so the reviews we facilitate come from firsthand knowledge of how decisions get made under pressure.
We don't stop at the report. We help organizations track follow-through on corrective actions so the lessons actually change how the next incident is run.
credentials_note: Includes consultants with Type 1 Incident Commander and Operations Section Chief Type 1 experience.

title: Business Development & Innovation
description: Advising investors, innovators, and founders bringing new technology, products, and services to the wildfire and emergency response industry.
summary: Advising investors, innovators, and founders bringing new technology, products, and services to the wildfire and emergency response industry.
body: The wildfire and emergency response industry is drawing real investment right now, from venture-backed platforms to established companies looking to bring new technology, products, and services into the space. Our consultants bring the inside perspective that pressure-testing those ideas requires, whether you're an investor evaluating an opportunity, a company developing new firefighting technology, or an individual working to start a venture of your own.

That means an honest look at business concept and market vetting: where the idea is strong, where it needs work, and what it will actually take to operate in this industry, from regulatory and certification pathways to who the real decision-makers are inside the agencies and companies that would actually buy or adopt it.

We work with investors and innovators evaluating the space, established companies developing new capabilities, and individuals and small teams at the earliest stages of a new venture, including startup planning, positioning, and introductions within the fire and aviation industry when they're useful.
